title: Reading the Equity Standing for an Estate Settlement of Membership and Patronage Equity
content:
What the equity standing is read from turns on what the equity ledger carries for the fiscal year the membership records as eligible for revolvement.

**Where a revolvement payment stands for that year.** Where a revolvement payment stands on the equity ledger for the fiscal year the membership records as eligible, the equity standing is the ledger's equity portions and capital retains less everything revolved out, rounded to two decimal places.

**Where none stands and a balance is recorded.** Where no such revolvement payment stands and an equity balance stands recorded on the membership above nothing, the equity standing is that recorded balance.

**Otherwise.** The equity standing is the ledger's equity portions and capital retains, nothing being taken off for revolvement, rounded to two decimal places.

## The three readings on hypothetical figures

Take equity portions of 11800.00 and capital retains of 1640.00 credited on the ledger, 1900.00 revolved out altogether, and an equity balance of 12000.00 recorded on the membership.

| What stands on the ledger for the eligible fiscal year | Equity standing |
| --- | --- |
| a revolvement payment | 11540.00 |
| none, with 12000.00 recorded on the membership | 12000.00 |
| none, with nothing recorded on the membership | 13440.00 |

**On the first reading.** What is taken off is everything revolved out on the membership, not only what was revolved against the eligible fiscal year; what the eligible year carries decides only which reading governs.

**On the second reading.** The recorded balance must stand above nothing. Where it stands at nothing, the last reading governs and the ledger is what the equity standing is read from. This is the reckoning Membership and Patronage Equity uses when an estate is settled.
